title: Harmonize idempotency header semantics and hedged-fanout limits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a concrete, interoperable spec and SDK primitives that standardize idempotency header semantics (TTL, scope, dedup window) and enforce safe hedged-request fanout limits tied to SLO tiers. This ticket covers spec, SDK changes (HTTP header helpers, client-side hedging config), runtime compatibility, and rollout plan.

Motivation: current services and SDKs use varied idempotency approaches (different header names, different deduplication windows) and hedging is uncontrolled in some clients leading to cascading resource blowups during region failover. Without a standard, multi-region failover becomes brittle: retries + unbounded hedges create high tail latency and can trip circuit breakers unnecessarily.

Proposed decisions: 
- Standard idempotency header name: X-Redwood-Idempotency (primary), accept Idempotency-Key as fallback for 12 months.
- Idempotency token semantics: token is opaque string; server dedup window = 120s default (configurable per route).
- Token scope: default = per-customer (tenant-scoped) for stateful endpoints; allow "global" flag for system-level dedup where necessary.
- TTL & storage: runtime will keep dedup entries for the configured window plus 5s slack to account for clock skew; recommend using LRU-backed stores with per-route caps.
- Client SDK helpers: generate v4 UUIDs and expose deterministic-sampling helper for low-impact read-only requests. 
- Hedged requests: default max_hedges = 1 (single additional speculative request) for P0 SLOs; 0 for extremely latency-sensitive single-shard calls. Max overall fanout multiplier = 2x for hedging; SDK must expose per-route override.
- Backoff profiles: map SLO tiers to retry/backoff/hedge: 
  * SLO-Low-Latency (p99 < 100ms): hedging-only, no retries; zipper fanout limit = 1 hedge, immediate speculative after 40ms tail threshold.
  * SLO-Standard (p99 < 500ms): exponential backoff with jitter, max retries=2, hedging allowed after first retry if latency > 200ms.
  * SLO-Bulk (throughput): larger initial backoff, no hedging, prefer queueing + load-shed.

- Circuit breakers: prefer sliding-window error-rate for open threshold, and additive backoff for short windows; hedging attempts count toward circuit metrics with lower weight (0.5) to avoid spurious opens.

Compatibility plan: runtime will accept both X-Redwood-Idempotency and Idempotency-Key for 12 months; SDKs will default to X-Redwood-Idempotency but include opt-in compatibility shim. Documentation and migration tooling will be provided.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change server-side dedup store implementation; it defines interfaces and runtime config knobs and SDKs. Implementation work split into follow-ups.

Links: Confluence spec draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/resilience/idempotency-hedging-spec, Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281 (WIP), SDK helper PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1532

acceptance_criteria: Reviewed spec with Reliability, Runtime, SDK, and Product — comments addressed
SDK release exposes X-Redwood-Idempotency header helper and toggles
Runtime accepts both headers and enforces dedup_window default=120s
Integration tests show no >15% increase in tail CPU/latency during hedged failover compared to baseline
Rollout plan with canary (10% traffic) documented and rollout playbook linked
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha: Initial draft posted on Confluence, flagged for security review due to header semantics. Asked Runtime owners for storage cost estimate.
2026-03-04 — Marco: Runtime prototype accepts X-Redwood-Idempotency and maintains dedup map with TTL; measured memory overhead ~0.8% for 120s window on our p3 configs.
2026-03-06 — Reliability (Priya Singh): Suggest reducing hedging concurrency during global region failover to avoid thundering herd; recommended adding per-customer hedging budget cap.
2026-03-08 — Design (Luca Marino): Approved header UX and migration messaging; asked SDKs to expose automatic idempotency generation but keep it opt-out for advanced users.
2026-03-10 — Marco: Updated runtime PR with weighted-hedge counting for circuit-breaker metrics (weight=0.5). Added integration test harness for simulated cross-region latency spikes.
